key_insight: SVR learns to use its own verdict and confidence as an internal control signal, so the model keeps refining only when it is not yet confident in a correct answer.
engineering_relevance: This enables adaptive test-time compute, reducing wasted reasoning steps on easy inputs while preserving accuracy without relying on external verifier feedback at inference.
method: Each turn: generate an answer plus a discrete correctness verdict and confidence score.
Retain the answer only if verdict = Correct and confidence exceeds a threshold; otherwise continue self-refinement.
Train with GRPO on fixed-horizon trajectories using rewards for correctness, calibration-aware self-verification, and stop-ready correct states.
evidence_signal: On seven mathematical reasoning benchmarks with Qwen3.5-2B, SVR reached a macro-average accuracy of 0.563 with just 2.99 inference turns on average.
watch_item: Performance depends on well-calibrated self-verification and thresholding, so miscalibration could cause premature stopping or unnecessary extra turns.
paper_title: SVR: Self-Verifying Refinement via Joint Verdict-Confidence Reinforcement Learning for Adaptive Test-Time Compute
